title: Gauss's Sum
hints: Adding all 100 numbers one by one works but takes a while. Is there a shortcut?
Try pairing numbers from opposite ends of the sequence: 1 + 100, 2 + 99, 3 + 98…
How many such pairs are there, and what does each pair sum to?
solution_lede:
The story goes that Carl Friedrich Gauss solved this as a schoolboy in seconds, while his classmates laboriously added each number. His insight: the sum has a beautiful symmetry you can exploit.

Pair the first and last terms: 1 + 100 = 101. Then 2 + 99 = 101. Then 3 + 98 = 101. Every pair sums to 101, and there are exactly 50 such pairs.

50 × 101 = 5050.

solution_steps.body: Pair each number with its mirror: 1+100, 2+99, 3+98, …, 50+51. Every pair sums to 101.
